  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that even the level of redemption through war is connected to the ultimate peaceful redemption, and that all levels of redemption contain the essence of self-sacrifice of the Yechidah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And perhaps one could say, on a deeper level,</t>
    <t s="2">that even the level of “redemption” that is through war,</t>
    <t s="3">since it is called by the name “redemption,”</t>
    <t s="4">it is connected to the redemption in peace</t>
    <t s="5">(even to the most exalted level that will be in the days of Moshiach in the second period).</t>
    <t s="6">And in the language of our Sages, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="7">“War is also the beginning of redemption,”</t>
    <t s="8">since</t>
    <t s="9">the name “redemption” applies to it.</t>
    <t s="10">Based on this, one can further explain the connection of the redemption of Yud-Tes Kislev and Yud-Tes Kislev with the verse “He redeemed my soul in peace,”</t>
    <t s="11">for at first glance,</t>
    <t s="12">behold, the course of events in the redemption of the Alter Rebbe is known,</t>
    <t s="13">and likewise in the redemption of the Mitteler Rebbe,</t>
    <t s="14">that they involved matters of subjugation,</t>
    <t s="15">effort, and the like,</t>
    <t s="16">i.e., matters of war,</t>
    <t s="17">and they connect this with the verse “He redeemed my soul in peace,” which refers</t>
    <t s="18">(as the Mitteler Rebbe explains in the aforementioned discourse)</t>
    <t s="19">to redemption in peace as it is in its ultimate perfection.</t>
    <t s="20">And one could say the explanation of this is:</t>
    <t s="21">that all the levels of redemption are connected to the redemption in peace in its ultimate perfection that will be in the future.</t>
    <t s="22">And this will be understood based on what the Baal HaGeulah explains in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="23">that the concept of “He redeemed my soul in peace” in the service of man</t>
    <t s="24">[that the redemption of the Nefesh HaElokis from the exile of the Nefesh HaBahamis is in a manner of peace,</t>
    <t s="25">where the Nefesh HaBahamis does not oppose at all]</t>
    <t s="26">is when the service is with mesirus nefesh,</t>
    <t s="27">and within mesirus nefesh itself—the mesirus nefesh of the Yechidah.</t>
    <t s="28">For through the mesirus nefesh that stems from Chayah,</t>
    <t s="29">only a subjugation of the Nefesh HaBahamis is accomplished,</t>
    <t s="30">but specifically through the mesirus nefesh that stems from Yechidah,</t>
    <t s="31">it is completely nullified.</t>
    <t s="32">Based on this, the connection of redemption through war</t>
    <t s="33">[the service that stems from Chayah,</t>
    <t s="34">and lower still, the service that stems from Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah]</t>
    <t s="35">to “He redeemed my soul in peace”</t>
    <t s="36">(Yechidah) will be understood,</t>
    <t s="37">because in every single service there is within it</t>
    <t s="38">(in a concealed manner)</t>
    <t s="39">the mesirus nefesh that stems from Yechidah.</t>
    <t s="40">And as it is stated in Tanya,</t>
    <t s="41">that engaging in Torah, mitzvos, and prayer is a matter of actual mesirus nefesh.</t>
    <t s="42">For since the true essence of the concept of mesirus nefesh</t>
    <t s="43">(actual mesirus nefesh)</t>
    <t s="44">is the mesirus nefesh that stems from Yechidah,</t>
    <t s="45">behold, it is found</t>
    <t s="46">that in every matter of Torah and mitzvos</t>
    <t s="47">[even the simple matters of Torah and mitzvos that, had the Torah not been given</t>
    <t s="48">(Heaven forbid),</t>
    <t s="49">they would have been learned from the beasts of the earth],</t>
    <t s="50">there is the power of the mesirus nefesh of the Yechidah.</t>
    <t s="51">And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="52">that even the understanding and comprehension of Torah is through the concept of the precedence of “we will do” to “we will hear,” as it is stated,</t>
    <t s="53">“The integrity of the upright guides them,”</t>
    <t s="54">for the concept of the precedence of “we will do” to “we will hear” is the nullification to the Master of the Will</t>
    <t s="55">(which is beyond the nullification to the will),</t>
    <t s="56">for this nullification comes from the essence of the soul</t>
    <t s="57">(which is beyond the revelations of the soul),</t>
    <t s="58">the level of Yechidah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that all levels of mesirus nefesh are essentially one, as they stem from the essence of the soul, and illustrates this with a parable of entering the army.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And although the concept of mesirus nefesh explained in the aforementioned maamar of the Baal HaGeulah is that all his desires are nullified</t>
    <t s="1">(to the extent that all matters are equal),</t>
    <t s="2">one could say</t>
    <t s="3">that all the levels of mesirus nefesh are one concept.</t>
    <t s="4">And analogous to what is known</t>
    <t s="5">regarding the concept of awe,</t>
    <t s="6">that since awe is nullification</t>
    <t s="7">(negation of existence),</t>
    <t s="8">therefore all the levels of awe are one awe,</t>
    <t s="9">so too one could say regarding the concept of the nullification of mesirus nefesh.</t>
    <t s="10">And moreover,</t>
    <t s="11">since the nullification of mesirus nefesh is from the totality and essence of the soul,</t>
    <t s="12">unlike the nullification of awe, which is only one attribute,</t>
    <t s="13">behold, this concept</t>
    <t s="14">[that all levels are one concept]</t>
    <t s="15">in mesirus nefesh is even greater than in awe.</t>
    <t s="16">And this will be understood through a parable from an earthly kingdom,</t>
    <t s="17">that when a person enters the army</t>
    <t s="18">(even though he has not yet served in the army,</t>
    <t s="19">and certainly has not been in battle),</t>
    <t s="20">he gives himself over completely, and he ceases to be his own master.</t>
    <t s="21">For so it is in the spiritual army,</t>
    <t s="22">that Israel are the “hosts of Hashem,”</t>
    <t s="23">for this that every Jew has acceptance of the yoke</t>
    <t s="24">[as per the well-known saying,</t>
    <t s="25">“A Jew is an acceptor of the yoke”],</t>
    <t s="26">that through this he enters the hosts of Hashem,</t>
    <t s="27">behold, through this he gives himself over completely to G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="28">and this giving over is connected to and illuminated by the mesirus nefesh that stems from the Yechidah at the most exalted level.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section resolves the apparent contradiction of the verse “He redeemed my soul in peace” being associated with prayer (a form of war), explaining that prayer also contains the mesirus nefesh that connects it to peaceful redemption.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">9)</t>
    <t s="1">Based on the above, one can also explain that which is stated in the Yerushalmi</t>
    <t s="2">on the verse “He redeemed my soul in peace… for many were with me,”</t>
    <t s="3">that it refers to the men of Avshalom who prayed for the welfare of Dovid.</t>
    <t s="4">For at first glance,</t>
    <t s="5">behold, it is explained above that redemption in peace is specifically through Torah, unlike prayer, which is through war,</t>
    <t s="6">and the prayer of the men of Avshalom was regarding the war of Avshalom.</t>
    <t s="7">And likewise, one must understand regarding the connection of the redemption of Yud-Tes Kislev with the verse “He redeemed in peace,”</t>
    <t s="8">behold, the redemption of the Alter Rebbe came about</t>
    <t s="9">(as he writes in his letter)</t>
    <t s="10">when he recited from the book of Tehillim,</t>
    <t s="11">and the nature of the recitation of Tehillim</t>
    <t s="12">(even though the book of Tehillim is among the twenty-four books of the Tanach,</t>
    <t s="13">Torah)</t>
    <t s="14">is prayer,</t>
    <t s="15">and in the language of the verse,</t>
    <t s="16">“the sweet singer of Israel”</t>
    <t s="17">(for songs are related to prayer),</t>
    <t s="18">and particularly based on what is known from the stories of our Nesi’im, that the redemption of the Alter Rebbe came about through the prayers of his students, chassidim, and all who followed in his footsteps,</t>
    <t s="19">and this redemption, which came through prayer,</t>
    <t s="20">“the time of prayer is the time of war,”</t>
    <t s="21">came about through the recitation of the verse “He redeemed in peace.”</t>
    <t s="22">And one could say the explanation of this is:</t>
    <t s="23">that since engaging in Torah and mitzvos is a matter of actual mesirus nefesh</t>
    <t s="24">(as brought above from Tanya),</t>
    <t s="25">therefore,</t>
    <t s="26">even prayer</t>
    <t s="27">is connected to “He redeemed in peace.”</t>
    <t s="28">And one could say,</t>
    <t s="29">that on the contrary,</t>
    <t s="30">the concept of mesirus nefesh is in prayer more than in Torah.</t>
    <t s="31">For this that engaging in Torah is actual mesirus nefesh,</t>
    <t s="32">behold, this feeling of mesirus nefesh must be “before he begins to study”</t>
    <t s="33">[and when he studies for many consecutive hours, he must contemplate this every hour],</t>
    <t s="34">but during the time of study,</t>
    <t s="35">when he is engaged in understanding and comprehending the subject he is learning,</t>
    <t s="36">he does not feel the nullification of mesirus nefesh.</t>
    <t s="37">And on the contrary, “Who is a king? The Rabbis,”</t>
    <t s="38">and “It is the Torah that excites him,”</t>
    <t s="39">unlike in prayer,</t>
    <t s="40">where one must be “like a servant before his Master,”</t>
    <t s="41">the ultimate nullification</t>
    <t s="42">(the nullification of mesirus nefesh).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
